_readme: Our own English translation of the Testament of Job, made for this app directly from
the Greek of manuscript P as transcribed by the Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, which
is public domain. Their eclectic texts of Brock and Kraft are licensed from Brill and
were NOT used; nor was Spittler's translation in Charlesworth, which is in copyright.
Keys are 'chapter.verse', matching the transcription's own numbering — the division
M. R. James established, which Brock and Charlesworth follow, so scholarly citations
P is an 11th-century witness with real irregularities: it spells Job's wife's name
variously across chapters and has occasional itacistic slips. The translation renders
the sense, normalising obvious slips; square brackets mark words supplied for sense.
build-tjob-greek.py hides English entirely until every verse is translated, so students
1.1: The book of the words of Job, who is called Jobab.
1.2: For on the day when he fell ill and was settling his affairs, he called his seven sons and his three daughters,
1.3: whose names are these: Tersi, Choros, Hyon, Nike, Phoros, Phiphe, Phrouon, Hemera, Kasia, and Amaltheia's Horn.
1.4: And when he had called his children he said: Gather round me, my children, gather round, so that I may show you what the Lord did with me, and everything that has happened to me.
1.5: For I am Job your father, who lived in all endurance; and you are a chosen and honoured race, from the seed of Jacob, the father of your mother.
1.6: For I am of the sons of Esau, the brother of Jacob, whose daughter Dinah is your mother, by whom I fathered you — for my former wife died a bitter death, together with ten other children. Listen to me then, my children, and I will make plain to you what has befallen me.
2.1: For I am Jobab, before the Lord named me Job.
2.2: When I was called Jobab, I lived at first very near an idol that was worshipped;
2.3: and seeing continually the whole burnt offerings brought up to it, I reasoned within myself and said:
2.4: Is this really the God who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and ourselves? How then am I to know?
3.1: And in the night, as I lay sleeping, a great voice came to me in a very great light, saying: Jobab! Jobab!
3.2: And I said: Here I am. And it said: Rise, and I will show you who this is whom you wish to know.
3.3: This one, to whom they bring whole burnt offerings and pour drink offerings, is not God; rather, this is the power of the devil, by which human nature is deceived.
3.4: And when I heard it I fell upon my bed, worshipping and saying:
3.5: My Lord, who have come for the salvation of my soul,
3.6: I beg you — if this is indeed the place of Satan, by which men are deceived — give me authority to go and cleanse his place,
3.7: so that I may put an end to the drink offerings poured to it. And who is there to prevent me, since I am king of this land?
4.1: And the light answered me and said: You will indeed be able to cleanse this place; but I am showing you everything that the Lord charged me to impart to you.
4.2: And I said: Whatever he has charged me — his servant — I will hear and do.
4.3: And again it said: These things says the Lord:
4.4: If you set about cleansing the place of Satan, he will rise against you in wrath for war — only that he will not be able to bring death upon you; but he will bring upon you many blows,
4.5: and he will take away your possessions, and will destroy your children.
4.6: But if you endure, I will make your name renowned in all the generations of the earth, until the consummation of the age.
4.7: And I will bring you back again to your possessions, and there shall be repaid to you double,
4.8: so that you may know that he shows no partiality, repaying good things to each one who obeys.
4.9: And you shall be raised up at the resurrection.
4.10: For you shall be like an athlete boxing and enduring hardship and awaiting the crown.
4.11: Then you will know that the Lord is just and true and strong, giving strength to his chosen ones.
5.1: And I, my little children, answered him: I will endure until death, and I will not draw back at all.
5.2: And after I had been sealed by the angel, who then went up from me, I rose in the following night, my little children, and taking fifty servants with me I went off to the temple of the idol and levelled it to the ground;
5.3: and so I withdrew into my house, having ordered the doors to be secured.
6.1: Listen to me, my little children, and marvel.
6.2: For as soon as I had gone into my house and secured my doors, I gave orders to my doorkeepers:
6.3: If anyone seeks me today, let no announcement be brought to me; but say to him: He is not free — he is inside, on urgent business.
6.4: And while I was inside, Satan, disguising himself as a beggar, knocked at the door
6.5: and said to the doorkeeper: Announce to Job that I wish to meet with him.
6.6: And the doorkeeper came in and told me this,
6.7: and she heard from me that she was to make plain that I was not free just then.
7.1: But Satan, hearing this, went away and laid a ragged cloak on his shoulders; and coming back he spoke to the doorkeeper, saying:
7.2: Say to Job: Give me bread from your own hands, that I may eat.
7.3: And I gave the servant girl a burnt loaf to give him, and I said to him:
7.4: Do not expect to eat of my bread any longer, for you have become a stranger to me.
7.5: And the doorkeeper, ashamed to hand him the burnt loaf, the colour of ashes —
7.6: for she did not know that he was Satan — took one good loaf of her own and gave it to him.
7.7: But he took it, and knowing what had happened said to the girl: Go, wicked servant, and bring me the loaf that was given you to give me.
7.8: And the girl wept with great grief, saying: You are quite right to call me a wicked servant;
7.9: for if I were not, I would have done as my master ordered me. And going back she brought him the burnt loaf, saying to him: These things says my lord:
7.10: You shall not eat of my bread any longer, because I have become a stranger to you;
7.11: yet I have given you even this, so that I may not be charged with giving nothing at all to an enemy who asked.
7.12: When Satan heard this he sent the girl back to me, saying: As this loaf is wholly burnt, so I will make your body too; for within a single hour I shall come and lay you waste.
7.13: And I answered him: Do what you will do; for whatever you mean to bring upon me, I am ready to endure whatever you inflict.
8.1: And when he had departed from me, he went away beneath the firmament
8.2: and put the Lord under oath, that he might receive authority over my possessions.
8.3: And then, having received the authority, he came and took away the whole of my wealth.
9.1: Listen then, for I will show you everything that has befallen me and all that was taken from me.
9.2: For I had a hundred and thirty thousand sheep,
9.3: and I set apart seven thousand of them to be shorn for the clothing of orphans and widows and the poor and the helpless. And I had a herd of eight hundred dogs that guarded my house;
9.4: and I had nine thousand camels, and from these I chose out three thousand to work in every city,
9.5: and having loaded them with goods I sent them to the cities and to the villages, charging them to go and give to the helpless and to the destitute and to all the widows.
9.6: And I had a hundred and thirty thousand grazing asses, and I set apart five hundred of them, and their offspring I ordered to be sold and given to the poor and the needy.
9.7: And they all came to meet me from every land. The four doors of my house stood open;
9.8: and I ordered my servants that these were to be kept open, with this purpose in view: that if any came asking alms and saw me sitting by one of the doors, they might not be ashamed and turn away with nothing; but when they saw me sitting at one door, they could go round by another and take as much as they needed.
10.1: And I had thirty tables set up in my house, standing at every hour for strangers alone;
10.2: and I had twelve other tables laid for the widows.
10.3: And if any stranger came forward asking alms, he had to be fed at the table before he received what he needed;
10.4: and I would not let him go out of my door with an empty lap.
10.5: And I had three thousand five hundred yoke of oxen, and from these I chose out five hundred yoke and set them to the ploughing which they could do in every field of those who took them,
10.6: and their produce I set apart for the poor, for their table.
10.7: And I had fifty bakeries, from which I appointed twelve for the service of the table of the poor.
11.1: And there were certain strangers too who, seeing my eagerness, desired themselves also to help in the service;
11.2: and there were others who were then without means, and unable to lay out anything, who came and entreated me, saying: We beg you — can we too carry out this service? Yet we possess nothing.
11.3: Do us this kindness and lend us gold, so that we may go off to the distant cities to trade, and be able to render service to the poor;
11.4: and afterwards we will restore your own to you.
11.5: And when I heard this I rejoiced, that they should take anything at all from me for the care of the poor;
11.6: and gladly, having taken the note of hand, I gave them as much as they wished,
11.7: taking no pledge from them but the written bond alone.
11.8: And so they traded with what was mine.
11.9: Sometimes their trading prospered, and they gave to the poor;
11.10: but sometimes they were robbed, and would come and entreat me, saying: We beg you, be patient with us, that we may see how we can make restitution to you.
11.11: And I, without delay, would bring out their bond and read it before them, and cancelling it would release them, saying: Since it was on the plea of the poor that I trusted you, I will take nothing from you.
11.12: And I would accept nothing from my debtor.
12.1: And if ever a man came to me cheerful at heart, saying: I am not well enough off to help the poor, yet I wish at least to serve the poor today at your table —
12.2: then, being permitted, he would serve and eat; and when evening came and he was going out to return to his house, he was compelled by me to take his wages, while I said to him:
12.3: I know that you are a working man, expecting and awaiting his wages; you must take them.
12.4: And I never let a hired man's wages remain with me in my house.
13.1: And those who milked the cows grew weary, for the milk flowed in the mountains;
13.2: and the butter ran down along my roads, and my cattle, because of their numbers, would lie down among the rocks and the mountains for their calving.
13.3: And on this account the mountains streamed with milk, and it stood like curdled butter.
13.4: And my servants also grew weary who boiled the food of the widows and the poor,
13.5: and in their impatience they would curse me, saying: Who will give us our fill of his flesh?
13.6: — and this though I was exceedingly kind to them.
14.1: And I had six psalms and a ten-stringed lyre;
14.2: and I would rouse myself each day, after the widows had been fed, and take up the lyre and play for them, and they would sing hymns.
14.3: And with the psaltery I would remind them of God, so that they might glorify the Lord.
14.4: And if ever my maidservants began to grumble, I would take up the psaltery and play them the wages of recompense,
14.5: and so I would put a stop to their impatient murmuring.
15.1: And my children, after the work of the service, would take their supper each day,
15.2: and they would go in to their eldest brother to dine with him,
15.3: taking their three sisters along with them; and what remained was for the maidservants.
15.4: For my sons used to recline together with the male servants who waited on them. So I would rise early in the morning and offer sacrifices on their behalf according to their number — three hundred doves, fifty kids of the goats, and twelve sheep;
15.5: and all these, over and above the fixed portion, I ordered to be prepared for the poor, and I would say to them: Take these as a surplus beyond the fixed portion, so that you may pray for my children.
15.6: For it might be that my sons had sinned before the Lord, boasting and saying in contempt:
15.7: We are the children of this rich man, and these goods are ours;
15.8: why then should we be servants? — for pride is an abomination before God.
15.9: And again I would offer a choice calf upon the altar of God, in case my sons had thought evil in their hearts toward God.
16.1: And while I was doing this, in the seven years after the angel had made his disclosure to me,
16.2: then, once Satan had received the authority, he came down without mercy
16.3: and burned up the seven thousand sheep that had been appointed for the clothing of the widows, and the three thousand camels and the five hundred asses and the five hundred yoke of oxen.
16.4: All these he consumed by his own hand, according to the authority he had received against me.
16.5: And the rest of my cattle were carried off by my own fellow citizens —
16.6: the very people who had received kindness from me, and who now rose against me and took away what livestock was left me.
16.7: And they reported to me the loss of my possessions; and I glorified God and did not blaspheme.
17.1: Then the devil, knowing my heart, contrived a plot against me;
17.2: and disguising himself as the king of the Persians he came upon my city, and gathered together all the crafty men in it,
17.3: and spoke to them with menace, saying: This man Jobab, who has spent all the good things of the earth and left nothing, who has distributed them to the needy and the blind and the lame —
17.4: he it is who pulled down the temple of the great god and destroyed the place of its drink offering. Therefore I too will repay him for what he did against the house of God. Come with me then, and let us plunder for ourselves all the beasts and everything he has upon the earth.
17.5: And they answered him: He has seven sons and three daughters; they might escape into other countries and lay charges against us as tyrants, and afterwards rise up and kill us.
17.6: And he said to them: Do not be afraid at all. Most of his possessions I have already destroyed by fire; the rest I have carried off — and now his children as well.
18.1: And when he had said this to them, he went off and threw the house down upon my children and killed them.
18.2: And my fellow citizens, seeing that what he had said had truly come to pass, came and drove me out and seized everything in my house.
18.3: My own eyes saw worthless and dishonoured men over my tables and my couches;
18.4: and I could not utter a word, for I was as helpless as a woman whose loins are slack from the multitude of her birth pangs,
18.5: remembering above all the war of which the Lord had forewarned me through his angel, and the praises that had been spoken to me.
18.6: And I became like a man wishing to enter a certain city, to see its wealth and inherit a share of its glory;
18.7: like a man with his cargo loaded on a seagoing ship, who out in mid-ocean sees the third great wave and the contrary winds, and throws his cargo into the sea, saying: I am willing to lose it all, only to enter this city, that I may inherit what is better than the ship and its gear.
18.8: So I too reckoned my own goods as nothing beside that city of which the angel had spoken to me.
19.1: And when the last messenger came and made known to me the loss of my children, I was shaken with a great shaking,
19.2: and I tore my garments, saying to the one who brought the news: How then were you saved?
19.3: And then, understanding what had happened, I cried out and said:
19.4: The Lord gave, the Lord has taken away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so it has come to pass. Blessed be the name of the Lord.
20.1: So when all my possessions had perished, Satan learned that he could not turn me to contempt;
20.2: and he went away and asked for my body from the Lord, that he might bring a plague upon me.
20.3: And then the Lord delivered me into his hands, to use my body as he wished; but over my soul he did not give him authority.
20.4: And he came upon me as I sat on my throne, mourning the loss of my children;
20.5: and he took the likeness of a great whirlwind and overturned my throne, and for three hours he held me down on my throne so that I could not get out.
20.6: And he struck me with a harsh plague from my feet to my head.
20.7: And in great trouble and distress I went out of the city, and sat down on the dunghill.
20.8: My body was eaten by worms; and I drenched the ground with the discharge, and the running of my body, and there were many worms in it.
20.9: And if ever a worm crawled off, I would take it up and put it back in the same place, saying: Stay in the place where you were set, until you are ordered elsewhere by the one who commanded you.
